title: Blessed Is the Man Who Fears the LORD

verses.text: Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments.
His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright— for the gracious, compassionate, and righteous.
It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice.
Surely he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever.
He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.
His heart is assured; he does not fear, until he looks in triumph on his foes.
He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.
The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the desires of the wicked will perish.

context.author: Not named. The twin of Psalm 111, with the same alphabet form; what Psalm 111 says of God, Psalm 112 says of the one who fears Him.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: “Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments” (v.1). His family is blessed and “his righteousness endures forever” (v.3), the very words Psalm 111:3 used of God. “Light dawns in the darkness for the upright” (v.4). “It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice” (v.5). He is steady: “He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD” (v.7). “He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor” (v.9). The wicked see it and grind their teeth, but their desires come to nothing (v.10).
context.custom: Lending to the poor without interest was commanded in the Law (Exodus 22:25; Deuteronomy 15:7-8). A horn lifted high (v.9) is a picture of strength and honor, from the horns of a wild ox. Bad news in the ancient world came by messenger, and a runner on the horizon could bring dread (2 Samuel 18:24-27).
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 113 begins the Hallel, the psalms of praise sung at Passover.
context.timelineBible: Paul quotes v.9 to encourage generous giving: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever” (2 Corinthians 9:9). Jesus said, “It is more blessed to give than to receive” (Acts 20:35). Paul told the Philippians not to be anxious but to pray, and the peace of God would guard their hearts (Philippians 4:6-7).

gospelParallels.note: More blessed to give than to receive.

otBackground.note: The same words said of God.
Open your hand to the poor.
Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD.

overview.summary: The one who fears the LORD reflects God’s own character: gracious, generous and just, unshaken by bad news, with a righteousness that endures forever.

history.t: Gifts for the poor in Jerusalem.

customs.t: Bringers of good or bad news.

archaeology.t: A 7th-century BC plea from a harvester to an official to return his confiscated cloak.
Stone shekel weights from Judah used in fair (or unfair) trade.

overview.discussion: “He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast” (v.7). What news do I dread, and what would steady my heart?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
